name: lspci
description: Lists all PCI devices: graphics cards, network controllers, storage controllers, USB controllers.

flags.description: Show kernel driver in use per device — the key troubleshooting flag.
Show numeric vendor:device IDs (for driver searches).

examples.output:
00:1f.6 Ethernet controller: Intel Corporation Ethernet Connection I219-V
03:00.0 Network controller: Intel Corporation Wi-Fi 6 AX200
examples.explanation: Finds network hardware. Here: wired Ethernet plus a Wi-Fi card.

examples.output:
01:00.0 VGA compatible controller: NVIDIA GA106 [GeForce RTX 3060]
  Kernel driver in use: nvidia
examples.explanation: Shows the GPU and WHICH driver the kernel loaded — the first check when graphics misbehave (nvidia vs nouveau).

about: lspci walks the PCI bus via /sys/bus/pci. The -k flag is the most valuable in practice: it reveals the driver bound to each device, which answers "is my hardware even detected and driven?" instantly.
useCases: Verify hardware detection after installing cards.
Find which driver a device uses.
Collect device IDs for driver research.
mistakes: Assuming hardware is broken when only the driver is missing — check lspci -k first.
